speaker: Mr David Hoe
text: asked the Minister for Social and Family Development (a) what proportion of the 2025 Child LifeSG Credits disbursed in July 2025 has not been utilised to date; and (b) where utilisation is lower than anticipated, whether the Ministry will consider extending the 12-month validity period while expanding outreach efforts to improve awareness.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: I am heartened to hear the take-up rate.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: In fact, it is a very good take-up rate.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is also what I observed in my house visits with residents.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: Against this backdrop, I have two supplementary questions.

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: First, does the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) have an initial sensing of the reasons for the 17% that have not started utilising the CLC?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: My second question is, through my house visits, would MSF also consider expanding the CLC to children beyond 12?

speaker: Mr David Hoe (Jurong East-Bukit Batok)
text: This is because parents often tell me that older children, like their teenagers, are at the phase of their life that they happen to eat more and this would also help to manage the household expenses and child-raising costs.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We have done public consultations, and we have heard feedback from parents, especially those of younger children, that in those ages, the diapers and the milk powder cost quite a bit more, and therefore the CLC was designed to better support our parents with young children on that front.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: So, I think that the Government, in that Budget announcement, has tried to do something for all our children and youths.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: On the other question on the utilisation rate, I thank the Member for the encouragement.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: I think is a healthy take-up rate, although there is still some ways to go.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: We do want the number to be higher, but we also note that there are some months left.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: There are various reasons for the portions yet to be used.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: In some cases, parents and families are still in the process of utilising it.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: They spread it out over the year, so we still have a couple of months.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Families leave it until the very last minute to claim and to use.

speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
text: Or in some cases, as the Member has pointed out, they may be simply unaware.
